examples.knowledge_point: Simplifying Rational Expressions Using an Alternate Form of the Pythagorean Identity
examples.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the denominator using $1-\cos^2 x = \sin^2 x.$ This gives

$$
\dfrac{\cos{x}}{1-\cos^2{x}} = \dfrac{\cos{x}}{\sin^2{x}}.
$$

Next, we simplify the expression by separating out the factors, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{{sin}^{2}⁡x} & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot 1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x} \\  & =\operatorname{cot}⁡x\operatorname{csc}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\dfrac{\cos{x}}{1-\cos^2{x}}=\cot{x}\csc{x}.
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we expand the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡x(\operatorname{sec}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{sec}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use the identity $\operatorname{sec}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}$ to further simplify the expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{sec}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡x & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}-{cos}^{2}⁡x \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}-{cos}^{2}⁡x \\  & =\frac{\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}{\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}-{cos}^{2}⁡x \\  & =1-{cos}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use the identity ${sin}^{2}⁡x=1-{cos}^{2}⁡x$ to rewrite the expression on the right-hand side.

Therefore, we conclude that:

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡x(\operatorname{sec}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)={sin}^{2}⁡x
$$
